headline: Semis and Software Take the Brunt as Monday's Session Ends in the Red
body_html:
Wall Street closed lower on Monday, September 28, as elevated oil prices and rising Treasury yields kept buyers on the sidelines across most of the market. Of the 544 names in our universe, 320 finished in the red versus 221 that managed a gain, underscoring the defensive tone of the session. Healthcare was the lone sector to close in positive territory, adding 0.45%, while every other group retreated.

The heaviest selling landed on semiconductors, which shed 1.75% as a group, and software, down 0.72%. The geopolitical backdrop — including fresh U.S.-Iran tensions and a suspected plot against a British airbase used by American forces — appeared to weigh on risk appetite while simultaneously pushing energy costs higher, pressuring companies sensitive to input prices. The Energy sector fell 1.01%.

MongoDB was the session's most dramatic story, tumbling 18.11% to lead all decliners. On the other side, ADMA Biologics surged 8.0% to pace all gainers, with Victoria's Secret and Gap Inc. advancing 7.23% and 5.93% respectively, suggesting selective appetite for consumer-apparel names even as the broader Consumer sector slipped 0.38%. The divergence between healthcare and everything else may be the session's most telling signal heading into the week.

briefs.headline: MongoDB Craters 18% in Session's Sharpest Single-Stock Move
briefs.body: MongoDB shed 18.11% on Monday, making it the steepest decliner across our entire universe. The database-software company's drop dragged on the broader software sector, which fell 0.72% on the day. No official company statement had been released by the close.

briefs.headline: Apparel Names Swim Against the Tide on a Down Day
briefs.body: Victoria's Secret and Gap Inc. rose 7.23% and 5.93% respectively, standing out sharply against a weak consumer-sector backdrop that finished down 0.38%. Burlington Stores added another 5.04%, signaling that value-oriented retail may be finding a bid even as discretionary spending concerns linger.

briefs.headline: Boeing 737 Max 10 Certification Hits Another Wall
briefs.body: The Federal Aviation Administration disclosed a software-related delay in the certification of Boeing's 737 Max 10, adding fresh uncertainty to the program's timeline. The news arrived on the same day analysts flagged the stock's recent dip as a potential entry point for longer-term investors.

briefs.headline: Iran War Overhang Lifts Oil, Hurts Stocks
briefs.body: Wall Street's retreat on Monday coincided with oil prices remaining elevated against a backdrop of active U.S.-Iran hostilities. UK diesel prices hit record highs as a direct result of the conflict, according to reports, while U.S. and Iranian officials were said to be preparing separate talks with mediators as early as Monday or Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Suspected Airbase Plot Rattles UK Security Establishment
briefs.body: British authorities arrested and later released five individuals on bail in connection with a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, a base also used by U.S. forces. Officials confirmed they are examining potential foreign state involvement, adding a layer of geopolitical unease that reverberated through risk markets on Monday.

briefs.headline: Russia's Military Budget Set for Sharp Climb in 2027
briefs.body: Budget documents reviewed by Reuters show Russia plans to raise military spending by 27% in 2027, a figure that analysts said underscores the durability of elevated defense outlays globally. The disclosure contributed to a cautious mood in equity markets already navigating the Iran conflict and rising energy costs.
